title: Closure of left and right lifting classes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category] and let $T$ be any class of its morphisms. A map $i:A\to B$ has the left lifting property against $p:X\to Y$ if for every $u:A\to X$ and $v:B\to Y$ with $pu=vi$ there is $h:B\to X$ with $hi=u$ and $ph=v$. Define ${}^{\square}T$ to be the class of maps with the left lifting property against every member of $T$, and $T^{\square}$ to be the class of maps against which every member of $T$ has the left lifting property. A map $f:A\to B$ is an arrow retract of $g:A'\to B'$ if there are $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $r:A'\to A$, $s:B'\to B$ satisfying $ga=bf$, $fr=sg$, $ra=1_A$ and $sb=1_B$. Then both ${}^{\square}T$ and $T^{\square}$ are closed under arrow retracts. The class ${}^{\square}T$ contains identities, is closed under composition of two composable members, and is closed under every pushout that exists, where a pushout is the colimit of a span [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
